title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 24-26): Grothendieck is building a purely combinatorial, order-theoretic model of a one-dimensional 'tame' space. A totally ordered set I plays the role of a segment, possibly with endpoints ω0 and ω1. From it he forms an ordered set M of 'cells': points a ∈ J, bounded open intervals J_{a,b}, half-lines J_{<a} and J_{>a}, and, in some cases, the whole open interval [J]. Elements of M are glued into 'trames' and 'figures' (cell decompositions); on the next page these lead to 'régions', 'polygones' and constructible parts.

The previous page treated three cases:
- M(I,∂I)∖{ω1}: half-open, with only J_{<a} added.
- M(I,∂I)∖{ω0}: with J_{>a} added.
- M(I,∂I)∖∂I = M(J), J = I∖∂I: this needs J_{<a}, J_{>a} (the 'traces' of I_{ω0,a} and I_{a,ω1}) and also a unit object [J] representing I_{ω0,ω1}.

This page justifies [J]. It is indispensable if one wants to express, as singular loci of a complete figure 𝓛_T (T a finite subset of J, written 'Parf(J)'), decompositions such as:
- {J_{<a}, J_{>a}} when T = {a};
- J_{<a}, J_{a,b}, J_{>b} when T = {a<b}.

When T = ∅ the complete figure must be the single open cell [J]. In modern terms, 𝓛_T is the stratification of an open interval by a finite set T of marked points: the strata are the points of T and the open complementary intervals. The poset M is the poset of all strata that occur in such stratifications.

He then insists that J = ∅ (i.e. I = {ω0,ω1}) must not be excluded. The trames in M then reduce to the single element [J], a 'trame' with one edge. Seen as a figure, it is an indivisible open interval, so that 'the indivisible open interval is represented by the empty ordered set!'. Here an open interval is encoded by the ordered set of its possible subdivision points, and an interval with no admissible cut points is encoded by ∅.

Unified formulation: data (I, Ω0, Ω1) with I ordered and Ω0, Ω1 ⊂ I, subject to:
- (a) every x ∈ Ω0 is the smallest element of I;
- (a') every y ∈ Ω1 is the largest element of I;
- (b) Ω0 ∩ Ω1 = ∅.

Hence card Ω0, card Ω1 ≤ 1, giving four cases: closed, the two half-open cases, and open. ∂I := Ω0 ∪ Ω1. The next page says that for regions, polygons and constructible sets no further hypothesis on I is needed. It then states a structure theorem: the M of a constructible polygon is a direct sum, over its connected components, of models of the form M(I,Ω0,Ω1).

Purpose: a combinatorial, model-theoretic foundation for 'topologie modérée' in dimension 1, i.e. the order-theoretic analogue of 1-dimensional cell decomposition, closed under restriction to constructible pieces.
errors: No substantive error. Condition (a) as written ('x is a smallest element') together with antisymmetry already forces card Ω0 ≤ 1, as the margin notes; similarly for Ω1.

Condition (b) excludes the degenerate case I = {pt} with ω0 = ω1; this is a deliberate choice (a closed interval has distinct ends). It is consistent with Joyal-type intervals but rules out a 'point-interval'.

'Un ordonné' presumably means totally ordered here (the notation J_{<a}, J_{a,b} and the interval picture require it), although the next page says no further hypotheses are needed for the theory of regions. Possibly ambiguous.
On p.26 Grothendieck himself flags an incomplete description ('Attention cette description est si 𝔓 ...'), so the general structure theorem is not finished in these notes.

ideas.what: Combinatorial model of a 1-dimensional stratified interval: poset M of cells (points, bounded open intervals, half-lines, whole open interval) built from an ordered set J. Figures 𝓛_T indexed by finite T ⊂ J give the stratification by T.
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition of a definable subset of a linear order (o-minimal 1-dim cell decomposition); face/exit-path poset of a stratified interval; interval algebra of a linear order
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984-86); exit-path categories: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (later)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6; this combinatorial model is unpublished

ideas.what: Insistence that the empty ordered set models the indivisible open interval (an open interval with no admissible subdivision points). This needs an extra 'unit' cell [J].
ideas.modern_name: Augmentation / empty totally ordered set as the open 1-cell; cf. augmented simplex category and the convention [−1] = ∅
ideas.where_published: Similar emphasis on not excluding the empty case appears in Pursuing Stacks, but this specific use is unsure

ideas.what: Triples (I, Ω0, Ω1): ordered set with optional bottom/top endpoint declared as boundary, distinct if both present. Four types: closed, two half-open, open. ∂I = Ω0 ∪ Ω1.
ideas.modern_name: Bipointed / partially pointed linear orders; generalisation of Joyal's 'intervals' (linear orders with distinct top and bottom, dual to Δ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joyal, 'Disks, duality and Θ-categories' (1997) for the closed case; folklore otherwise

missed.claim: Grothendieck's triples (I,Ω0,Ω1) with Ω0∩Ω1=∅ contain, as the closed case, exactly Joyal's intervals (linear orders with distinct bottom and top), whose category is dual to Δ. He also adds the open and half-open cases, with the open interval encoded by J = I∖∂I (empty allowed). This is an early, independent use of 'interval' objects with prescribed endpoints as the combinatorial basis of 1-dimensional geometry. In 1986 it was framed for tame topology / constructible sets rather than for simplicial duality.
missed.quote: il faut dire qu'on se donne (I, Ω0, Ω1) avec I, un ordonné ; Ω0, Ω1 ⊂ I et les conditions a) ... b) x ∈ Ω0, y ∈ Ω1 ⇒ x ≠ y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly: a four-type interval category might give a uniform combinatorial treatment of open, closed and half-open strata in exit-path / stratified homotopy theory. Content-wise it is elementary.

missed.claim: The pages develop a purely order-theoretic theory of constructible sets, polygons and 'régions' over an arbitrary ordered set. It includes a decomposition theorem (M of a constructible polygon is a direct sum of models M(I,Ω0,Ω1)), left incomplete on the next page.
missed.quote: l'intervalle ouvert indivisible est représenté par l'ensemble ordonné vide !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own attempt at combinatorial foundations of tame topology, which is historically interesting. Mathematically, the 1-dimensional case is covered by o-minimality / interval algebras.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary but carefully conceived bookkeeping step in an unpublished combinatorial approach to 1-dimensional tame topology. Of historical interest as evidence of how Grothendieck pursued the Esquisse tame-topology programme in 1986. The mathematics (interval types, empty order as open cell) is routine and well covered by o-minimality and Joyal-type interval duality.
transcription_corrections: Line 2-3: '[-Dans-] Le cas où' — 'Dans' is struck through; the reading 'Le cas où I = {ω0, ω1} correspond au cas où J = ∅' is right.
'Les trames dans M se réduit au seul élément [J]' — likely 'se réduisent'. The next phrase is probably 'La trame [singleton] réduite à une seule arête', i.e. the trame consisting of a single edge.
The struck word before 'x ∈ Ω0' in condition a) is a crossed-out symbol (likely a quantifier), not part of the statement.
'Parf(J)' plausibly denotes the set of finite parts of J (parties finies); the symbol 𝓛_T may be a script 'L' or 'F' for the complete figure.
'singularités [?]' — the word is struck through/overwritten in the image; the sense is 'singular loci' / decomposition pieces of a complete figure.
